svg.title: Standing waves and boundary conditions
svg.desc: Two columns compare displacement standing waves. A string fixed at both ends has displacement nodes at both endpoints and supports harmonics 1, 2, and 3, with wavelengths 2L, L, and 2L/3. An ideal air pipe closed at the left and open at the right has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. Its first three modes are harmonics 1, 3, and 5, with wavelengths 4L, 4L/3, and 4L/5. Filled blue circles mark displacement nodes and outlined orange circles mark displacement antinodes. Solid and dashed curves show opposite phases. Air displacement is longitudinal; curve height represents signed displacement, not a transverse air motion or a pressure profile.
svg.text: The allowed wavelengths follow from the motion permitted at each end.
Each curve shows displacement along a system of length L; the two shapes are half a cycle apart.
Opposite phases of the same mode
In an air column, a displacement node is a pressure antinode, and a displacement antinode is a pressure node.
Air motion is longitudinal. Curve height represents signed air displacement; these are not pressure profiles.
The closed-open pipe supports only odd harmonics under ideal boundary conditions; end corrections are neglected.
